record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one show that test particles, modeled as very small but finite bodies, move along spacetime geodesics?

evidence.quote: Show that test particles (very small, but finite, bodies) move on spacetime geodesics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth $4$-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the Einstein field equations, and consider a one-parameter family of "small bodies" modeled as compactly supported energy-momentum tensors $T^{ab}_\varepsilon$ on $M$ that satisfy appropriate energy conditions (e.g., the dominant energy condition), are conserved ($\nabla_a T^{ab}_\varepsilon = 0$), and whose spatial supports shrink to a timelike curve $\gamma$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, while the bodies remain "test" in the sense that their self-gravitational effect on the background geometry is negligible in a precise limit sense.

Prove (or disprove) the following statement: any such curve $\gamma$ arising as the limit worldline of a sequence of very small but finite (extended) bodies in $(M,g)$ must be, up to reparametrization, a timelike geodesic of the Lorentzian metric $g$.

In other words, formulate a rigorous theorem showing that test particles, modeled as very small but finite bodies whose stress-energy is conserved and satisfies physically reasonable energy conditions, move along geodesics of the ambient spacetime.
artifact.category_tag: General relativity / geodesic motion of small bodies
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous partial results exist: the Geroch–Jang theorem (1975) shows that smooth curves contained in arbitrarily small bodies satisfying suitable energy conditions are timelike geodesics, and Gralla–Wald and more recently Geroch–Weatherall ("The Motion of Small Bodies in Space-Time", Comm. Math. Phys. 2018) have extended this to formulations including self-gravitating small bodies and charged bodies. A fully general theorem under minimal hypotheses (including back-reaction and matter models) remains an active area of refinement, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Motion of Small Bodies in Space-Time
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on the motion of small bodies in general relativity has captured a sense in which such bodies follow timelike geodesics (or Lorentz-force curves if charged).
status_evidence.claim: Theorems exist confirming that small bodies follow geodesics under suitable hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: On the Status of the Geodesic Principle in General Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: The Geroch-Jang theorem states that if a smooth curve can be contained within arbitrarily small bodies satisfying certain energy conditions, then the curve is a timelike geodesic.
status_evidence.claim: Geroch–Jang gives a rigorous partial answer to the geodesic principle.
